lens: Layout and typography. All fourteen crops visually inspected. Responsive/accessibility scores cover visible fit and readability only; interaction, contrast ratios, target sizes and semantics were not measured. Parent padding is excluded from judgment.

findings: Before hierarchy 8: 'Accounts' blends into the adjacent metadata. Give the section name stronger weight; the after image implements this.

Before and after typography/numbers 8: the quota descriptions and loaded/eligible counts are small beside the bold percentages. Increase those secondary labels one type-size step while retaining the percentage emphasis.
The after image gives account names and detail lines slightly more separation from their chevrons. The three-column alignment and visible values remain consistent. No score drops.
Before hierarchy 8: strengthen the 'Accounts' heading relative to 'Weekly Remaining' and the counts; the after image resolves this.
Before and after typography/numbers 8: 'Cloud Session Credits · Low' and '5-Hour Limit · Low' remain small. Increase their text size one step, keeping the values right-aligned.
All three account names, percentages and warning lines fit without visible collisions. The added text inset remains workable at this width. No score drops.
Before hierarchy 8: the section title has the same emphasis as its descriptor. Use the stronger 'Accounts' weight visible in the after image.
Before and after typography/numbers 8: warning descriptions and the loaded/eligible line are small. Increase those labels one type-size step, allowing row height to grow if needed.
The stacked account rows retain clear separators, aligned percentages and a distinct Expand All control. No visible clipping or score drops.

Before and after hierarchy 8: 'Weekly quota unavailable' competes with the account name because it is larger than the other status descriptions. Reduce it to the secondary status-text size while retaining its amber colour and explicit wording.

Before and after typography/numbers 8: the long account name wraps legibly, but the smaller quota labels create an uneven type scale beside the unavailable message. Standardize secondary status text at a slightly larger shared size.
Before and after consistency 8: the unavailable message and Low messages use visibly different type sizes. Apply one secondary-status treatment to both.
The after heading is stronger. The three-line account name, percentage, unavailable dash and warning values remain visible. No score drops.
Before hierarchy 8: make 'Accounts' distinct from the metadata; the after image supplies the stronger weight.
Before content 8: 'Unavailable' does not identify the missing quantity. Use 'Weekly quota unavailable'; the after image implements this clarification.
Before and after typography/numbers 8: the warning labels and header counts remain small. Increase these secondary labels one type-size step.
The after image preserves the unavailable dash and the other accounts' displayed values. The longer status still fits within its column. No score drops.
Before hierarchy 8: strengthen the section heading; the after image resolves this.
Before layout 8: Stale occupies a separate line above the observation timestamp, making this account taller. Place Stale beside the account name while retaining the timestamp beneath it.
After layout 8: placing Stale after 82.8% shifts the percentage inward relative to the other accounts. Put Stale beside the account name and restore the percentage to the shared right edge.
Before and after typography/numbers 8: warning labels and the observation timestamp are small. Increase secondary text one type-size step.
Consistency drops from 9 to 8 because the after image breaks the shared right-edge alignment of the headline percentages. Restore that alignment without removing the stale status or timestamp.
The after image reduces the section height while preserving the visible stale value and observation time.

Before and after hierarchy 8: 'Current' is visually similar to the metric labels beneath it. Give this subsection label medium weight so the metric group is easier to distinguish from the observation and forecast details below.
Before and after typography/numbers 8: reset timestamps and lower metadata labels are small across all three columns. Increase their type size one step while preserving the aligned numeric columns.
The after image strengthens 'Accounts' and increases the inset beside the disclosure chevrons. Progress bars, percentages and the lower information grids retain their alignment.
The visible metric values, reset times, observation times and forecasts are preserved. No score drops.
